title: When Bad Social Practices Drive Out Good
author: Renn, Aaron
summary: Renn applies Gresham's Law—bad money drives out good—to social and cultural practices within organizations and communities. When unhealthy relationship patterns, toxic behaviors, or destructive values gain cultural momentum, they can displace healthier alternatives that people actually prefer. This happens in organizations, communities, and broader culture when not actively managed. Reversing this dynamic requires intentional cultivation of good practices, not just resistance to bad ones. Leaders must actively strengthen healthy cultures or risk losing them.
points: Gresham's Law applies to social practices: toxic behaviors can displace healthy ones if left unchecked.
Unhealthy relationship patterns gain momentum and become normalized when not actively resisted.
Simply opposing bad practices is insufficient; good practices must be actively cultivated.
Culture drifts toward lower standards if healthy norms aren't deliberately reinforced.
Leadership requires protecting cultural health through constant cultivation of good practices.
The effort to maintain healthy culture is constant because corrosive forces are always present.
